name: GA-08
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbent Austin Scott running with large financial advantage
Democratic challenger Kelly Esti raised only ~$19k with minimal cash
Prediction markets price Republican win at ~97%
model.rationale: Austin Scott holds a heavily Republican rural Georgia seat with a decisive money edge, while Kelly Esti's campaign is essentially unfunded and no polls suggest competitiveness; markets price this as a near-certain Republican hold.
model.watch: A surprise wave election or unexpected incumbent scandal could narrow the margin, though nothing in the current evidence points that way.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Austin Scott is seeking another term in a south Georgia district that leans Republican by about fifteen points. He enters the general election with more than $1.3 million on hand, while Democratic challenger Kelly Esti has raised under $20,000 and has almost no cash remaining. No independent polls or expert ratings exist for the race, and prediction markets give Scott roughly a 97 percent chance of winning.

The fundamentals point the same direction: the district's partisan lean, incumbency advantages, and the lopsided fundraising gap all favor Scott. Absent an extraordinary external shock, this race is expected to remain firmly in Republican hands.
